milestones.name: Open a company account and decide which employees can approve what
Get a public business profile with a credit rating buyers can check
Sell an unpaid invoice and get the cash today instead of in 60 days
Know the payout will happen on the due date without chasing anyone
Build a track record that makes the next invoice cheaper to sell
Get approved to invest and set the fund's own limits on what it can buy
Buy an unpaid invoice at a discount
Sell part of it early instead of waiting for the due date
Get paid when the invoice is settled

goals.statement: Open a company account and decide which employees can approve what
Get a public business profile with a credit rating buyers can check
Sell an unpaid invoice and get the cash today instead of in 60 days
Know the payout will happen on the due date without chasing anyone
Build a track record that makes the next invoice cheaper to sell
Get approved to invest and set the fund's own limits on what it can buy
Buy an unpaid invoice at a discount
Sell part of it early instead of waiting for the due date
Get paid when the invoice is settled

steps.trigger: Ironline Freight needs an account for the business, not for a person
steps.action: Opens the company account that holds Ironline Freight's money
steps.outcome: the money belongs to the company, not to whoever happened to set it up
steps.whyStack: The company owns the money, not the employee who set it up.
steps.requirement: Create or use at least one Privy wallet
steps.whyWins: Signs as a company, not as one person's key.

steps.trigger: one employee acting alone could sell an invoice that does not exist
steps.action: Decides who can sell an invoice: the office manager up to $10,000, two directors above that
steps.outcome: small invoices move without fuss, big ones need a second person to agree
steps.whyStack: Different limits for different staff on one account.
steps.requirement: Use at least one Privy control, such as policies, signers, key quorums, or intents
steps.extraPoints: Privy names: policies and team permissions
steps.whyWins: An org chart, not a single multisig.

steps.trigger: investors will not fund a company they have never heard of
steps.action: Claims a public business profile at ironline.receivables.eth
steps.outcome: anyone can look Ironline Freight up before deciding to fund them
steps.whyStack: Reputation the business carries anywhere, not locked in our database.
steps.requirement: Project must be built on ENSv2 (Sepolia)
steps.extraPoints: Your own subname registry, run under your own rules
steps.whyWins: The record outlives the relationship with us.

steps.trigger: a rating a company writes about itself is worth nothing
steps.action: Hands the credit rating on that profile to an independent reviewer to set
steps.outcome: Ironline Freight can never raise its own rating, and the reviewer can change nothing else
steps.whyStack: They own the profile; someone independent sets the rating.
steps.requirement: ENSv2 features should be central to the product, not a cosmetic add-on
steps.extraPoints: Enhanced Access Control — a role scoped to one text record
steps.whyWins: On camera: the business tries to raise its own rating and is refused.

steps.trigger: a freight broker owes Ironline Freight $50,000 on 60-day terms
steps.action: Two directors approve the sale from their phones, hours apart
steps.outcome: the sale goes ahead on its own the moment the second approval lands
steps.whyStack: Approvals collected from people who are never online together.
steps.requirement: Implement at least one functional B2B workflow, such as a payment, approval, treasury operation, or wallet administration flow
steps.extraPoints: Privy names: quorum approvals and intents
steps.whyWins: Timestamps hours apart — most teams demo both approvals ten seconds apart.

steps.trigger: the invoice is approved for sale
steps.action: The invoice becomes something an investor can buy: $50,000, payable in 60 days
steps.outcome: the claim on that invoice now exists on its own, separate from Ironline Freight
steps.whyStack: An invoice with a due date and holder rules; a plain token has neither.
steps.requirement: Use the Asset Tokenization Studio (SDK, contracts, web application, or a combination) to issue or manage a tokenised asset
steps.whyWins: A real due date and a real obligor, not a token with a name on it.

steps.trigger: at this point anyone at all could buy it
steps.action: Locks the invoice so only approved investors can ever own it
steps.outcome: an unapproved buyer is turned away even if they try to go around the app
steps.whyStack: The rule lives in the invoice, so it holds outside our app.
steps.requirement: Demo video of five minutes or less showing issuance, configuration, and at least one lifecycle operation such as a transfer, compliance check, or distribution
steps.extraPoints: Compliance controls in use: KYC grants, freezes, transfer restrictions, pauses
steps.whyWins: The refusal is visible on HashScan, not a greyed-out button.

steps.trigger: payday is 60 days out and nobody should have to remember it
steps.action: Books the day-60 payout now, at the moment of sale
steps.outcome: the payout happens on its own, even if Ironline Freight and this app are both long gone
steps.whyStack: The payout fires even if we no longer exist.
steps.requirement: Deploy and demonstrate on Hedera testnet
steps.extraPoints: Scheduled Transactions for vesting, coupon payments, or maturity settlement
steps.whyWins: Settlement cannot be forgotten; it was booked at the sale.

steps.trigger: day 60 arrives and the broker has paid
steps.action: Everyone who owns a piece of the invoice is paid their share
steps.outcome: the $50,000 reaches whoever owns it that day, split correctly
steps.whyStack: Pays whoever owns it on the day, split correctly.
steps.requirement: Demo video of five minutes or less showing issuance, configuration, and at least one lifecycle operation such as a transfer, compliance check, or distribution
steps.extraPoints: Custom fee schedules, coupon or dividend distributions, royalty flows
steps.whyWins: A real corporate action at maturity, not a one-shot mint.

steps.trigger: the invoice was paid on time
steps.action: Ironline Freight's public profile gains one more invoice paid on time
steps.outcome: the next invoice sells at a better rate because of it
steps.whyStack: A funder who has never used us can check the record.
steps.requirement: Your demo must be functional and not just include hard-coded values
steps.whyWins: Written by the redemption, read back to price the next sale.

steps.trigger: a fund has cash sitting idle and wants short, secured returns
steps.action: Signs up and is ready to invest, with no crypto wallet to install
steps.outcome: the fund can buy and get paid without anyone handling a seed phrase
steps.whyStack: A fund invests without anyone handling a seed phrase.
steps.requirement: Create or use at least one Privy wallet
steps.whyWins: One control plane serves a small carrier and an institutional fund.

steps.trigger: the fund's investment rules live in a document nobody checks in time
steps.action: Writes the fund's rules in: never more than $100,000 on one invoice, never below a B rating
steps.outcome: an investment that breaks the fund's own rules simply will not go through
steps.whyStack: The fund's own rules block the trade instead of catching it next week.
steps.requirement: Use at least one Privy control, such as policies, signers, key quorums, or intents
steps.extraPoints: Privy names: policies and automated transactions
steps.whyWins: On camera: an allocation over mandate is refused.

steps.trigger: only approved investors are allowed to own these invoices
steps.action: Woodgrove is issued an approval pass with an expiry date
steps.outcome: the pass lapses on its own, can be withdrawn, and is useless to anyone Woodgrove hands it to
steps.whyStack: Approval that expires, can be withdrawn, and cannot be passed on.
steps.requirement: ENSv2 features should be central to the product, not a cosmetic add-on
steps.whyWins: Three named ENSv2 features in one name, each true of real KYC.

steps.trigger: the invoice itself has to recognise the pass
steps.action: The approval pass is copied across to where the invoices are held
steps.outcome: Woodgrove can now be handed an invoice
steps.whyStack: The invoice itself has to recognise the approval to enforce it.
steps.requirement: Use the Asset Tokenization Studio (SDK, contracts, web application, or a combination) to issue or manage a tokenised asset
steps.extraPoints: Compliance controls in use: KYC grants, freezes, transfer restrictions, pauses
steps.whyWins: The cross-chain hop is the integration, not a gap.

steps.trigger: Woodgrove goes to buy Ironline Freight's invoice
steps.action: Woodgrove is checked at the moment of purchase, not beforehand
steps.outcome: an approved buyer receives it; anyone else is refused, even going around the app
steps.whyStack: The rule applies on every route in, including apps we did not build.
steps.requirement: Demo video of five minutes or less showing issuance, configuration, and at least one lifecycle operation such as a transfer, compliance check, or distribution
steps.extraPoints: Compliance controls in use: KYC grants, freezes, transfer restrictions, pauses
steps.whyWins: Reverts on-chain — a front-end gate is worth nothing to a regulated buyer.

steps.action: Pays $47,500 and takes ownership of the invoice
steps.outcome: Ironline Freight has cash today; Woodgrove is owed $50,000 in 60 days
steps.whyStack: Predictable settlement cost, when the whole margin is a small discount.
steps.requirement: Deploy and demonstrate on Hedera testnet
steps.whyWins: A testnet transaction a judge can open.

steps.trigger: Woodgrove wants its cash back before day 60
steps.action: Puts half the invoice up for sale to other approved investors
steps.outcome: the half is on offer without waiting for the broker to pay
steps.whyStack: A half-share sells on without losing the rule about who may own it.
steps.requirement: Use the Asset Tokenization Studio (SDK, contracts, web application, or a combination) to issue or manage a tokenised asset
steps.extraPoints: A secondary market for ATS-issued assets, which the Studio does not have today
steps.whyWins: First item on the track's own extra-points list; ATS ships nothing like it.

steps.trigger: another approved investor takes the offer
steps.action: That half changes hands, with the new buyer checked the same way
steps.outcome: Woodgrove has cash back on day 20, and the invoice now has two owners
steps.whyStack: The rule survives a sale we had nothing to do with.
steps.requirement: Demo video of five minutes or less showing issuance, configuration, and at least one lifecycle operation such as a transfer, compliance check, or distribution
steps.extraPoints: A secondary market for ATS-issued assets, which the Studio does not have today
steps.whyWins: Resale is where restricted assets normally leak.

steps.trigger: day 60 arrives and the broker has paid
steps.action: Both owners are paid their share without either of them doing anything
steps.outcome: each is paid in proportion to the piece they hold
steps.whyStack: Both owners paid correctly after the invoice was split.
steps.requirement: Demo video of five minutes or less showing issuance, configuration, and at least one lifecycle operation such as a transfer, compliance check, or distribution
steps.extraPoints: Custom fee schedules, coupon or dividend distributions, royalty flows
steps.whyWins: Two owners after the split, both paid correctly.
